lead.text: Another one. Moss closed a €35m Series C led by Portage at a valuation north of €1bn — Europe's newest unicorn on the day Sifted wrote it up, and Germany's newest on any reading. Ante Spittler and his three co-founders started in 2019 selling corporate cards to mid-market finance teams; the company now sits between those teams and every euro that leaves the business, with the receipt, the approval and the ERP line attached to each one. That is a boring, enormous job, and Berlin's fintech bench keeps producing companies willing to do it rather than chasing the consumer app. Moss is already in this register — its entry carries this round and the crossing it produced.

source.title: Moss hits a €1 billion valuation and bets on Finance AI shaped by finance teams

lead.text: NavVis raised €73.7m in a Series D led by the American private equity firm The Jordan Company, thirteen years after four researchers spun it out of the Technical University of Munich. It maps the inside of buildings — factories, plants, the mission-critical infrastructure nobody photographs — and keeps the digital copy synchronised with the physical one; Felix Reinshagen says customers trust it with billions of square metres of that data. This is the German pattern in a single line: a decade of unfashionable engineering, a growth round from abroad, and the company still headquartered in Munich.

source.title: Munich-based NavVis raises €73.7 million to build its spatial data engine and accelerate AI roadmap
